newsitem.title: FRANCE: Protesters want French immigration reforms dropped.
newsitem.headline: Protesters want French immigration reforms dropped.

text.p: About 3,000 people marched through the streets of Paris on Saturday to try to persuade the government to drop plans to tighten already tough laws against illegal immigration.
Separately, 200 people demonstrated in Toulouse, southern France, urging that a group of African immigrants lacking residence papers be allowed to remain legally in France.

Organisers of the Paris march said the immigration bill, which was approved by the National Assembly last month but has not yet been taken up by the Senate, violated human rights and would turn immigrants and their friends into criminals.
One controversial provision of the bill would restrict an individual's freedom to put up a foreigner temporarily in a private residence.
Another would unconditionally bar an illegal immigrant from obtaining a residence permit, no matter how long the immigrant had lived in France.
The bill is part of a government crackdown on the estimated one million illegal immigrants -- known as "sans-papiers" because they lack residence papers -- among France's five million foreigners.
The effort was marred by the government's decision last year to order police to forcibly evict several hundred Africans, most of them lacking residence permits, from their refuge in a Paris church.
Most of those seized in the raid were later spared when magistrates thwarted orders to expel them. The new law would prevent a repeat of that situation by tying magistates' hands in such cases.

Of the 324 sans-papiers who occupied the church for nearly two months last summer, 103 ended up obtaining residency papers, 19 were expelled, two were in prison, one died from a liver cancer and 199 others were still in legal limbo, according to a tally published on Saturday by the French daily Liberation.
